mainEvent.title: Thu 11/19 · Anthropic jumps 17% in its debut, but the Dow sinks 1,101
mainEvent.body: Anthropic (**ANT**) first traded at **$111.50** at 11:48a, 34% above its $83 IPO price, touched about $115, then faded to a $92.72 low and closed at **$97.17**, up **17%**, on about 830–840 million shares (StockTitan, FinanceFeeds, Yahoo Finance). The debut did not lift the AI trade: the S&P 500 fell **2.0%** for a sixth straight loss, the Nasdaq **2.3%**, and the Dow **1,101 points** to 49,097, closing below 50,000, as AMD, Amazon, Alphabet and Nvidia slid and all 11 sectors fell (Yahoo Finance, Reuters). The VIX jumped 15.8% to **28.44** (Cboe). After the bell Intuit fell about 11% on a light Q2 outlook and Ross about 9%. Friday: Fed's Waller at 8:25a, final UMich sentiment at 10:00a, monthly options expiration, and December WTI expires.

stories.title: Dow sinks 1,101 points below 50,000; S&P 500 falls a sixth day.
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell **2.02%** to 7,175.83 Thursday, its sixth straight loss, the Nasdaq **2.25%** to 23,879.20 and the Dow **1,101.11 points** (2.19%) to 49,097.06, closing below 50,000; the Russell 2000 lost about 1.8% (Yahoo Finance, Reuters via MarketScreener). Futures had been up about 1% before the open, but selling picked up once Anthropic began trading, as investors took profits in AI names (CNBC via StockTitan). AMD fell **7.7%** after Hunterbrook disclosed a short position citing its China exposure (Reuters, Yahoo Finance); Amazon lost 3.9%, Alphabet 3.5%, Nvidia 3.3% and Microsoft 2.0%, while CoreWeave fell 6.1% and Nebius 9.4% (StockTitan). All 11 sector ETFs fell, with consumer discretionary (XLY −2.8%) and communication services (XLC −2.7%) worst and energy (XLE −0.7%) the most resilient. Williams-Sonoma dropped 15% after its results; Palo Alto (+6.4%), CrowdStrike (+2.7%) and PDD (+11%) rose. The VIX jumped 15.8% to **28.44** (Cboe), and CNN's Fear & Greed index fell to 18.7, extreme fear, from 40 a week ago.

stories.title: Anthropic closes up 17% at $97.17 after opening at $111.50.
stories.body: Anthropic's shares first traded at **$111.50** at 11:48a, 34% above the $83 IPO price, and touched about $115 within a minute before sliding to a $92.72 low at 1:18p; they closed at **$97.17**, up **17.1%**, on about 830–840 million shares, close to the 980 million sold in the IPO (StockTitan, FinanceFeeds, Yahoo Finance). The stock slipped to about $95.70 after hours (Yahoo Finance). The company raised about **$81.3B**, the largest IPO ever, plus a $26B private placement at $83 with Nvidia, Google and others (StockTitan, Reuters). Market value at the close is about $1.3 trillion on shares outstanding (Nasdaq via FinanceFeeds), or about $1.8 trillion fully diluted (Reuters, CNN); the fade from the opening print erased nearly $200B (Yahoo Finance). Dan Ives called the deal an "A-plus success" (via FinanceFeeds), but the listing did not lift its big backers: Amazon and Alphabet both fell more than 3%.

stories.title: Fed: hikes still priced as Goolsbee warns AI could overheat the economy.
stories.body: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said Thursday that AI data-center building and consumers spending out of new stock wealth "can easily overheat the economy" and that "the Fed's job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy" (Reuters via Kitco). Minutes of the Oct 27–28 meeting showed **almost all** officials saw more hikes as likely appropriate and **a couple** were open to more than 25bp in December (TheStreet, investingLive), and Governor Waller said this week a half-point move is probably needed. The data keep softening: the Philly Fed index fell to 6.3 from 20.9 vs about 20 expected (Trading Economics, FX.co), jobless claims rose to 203K vs 197K (Labor Department), and the Conference Board's leading index fell **0.3%** in October vs no change expected, mostly on fewer building permits (RTTNews, Bloomingbit). The 10Y ended about 1bp lower at 5.05%. CME FedWatch put about 10% on a 50bp December move Wednesday (TheStreet). Waller speaks again Friday at 8:25a. The next decision is Dec 9; Kalshi has a 25bp hike at 91% and more than 25bp at 6%.

stories.title: Intuit falls 11% after hours on a light outlook; Ross, Gap disappoint.
stories.body: Intuit's fiscal Q1 revenue rose 12% to **$4.35B** vs about $4.31B expected, with non-GAAP EPS of **$2.91** (it no longer excludes stock pay), but it guided Q2 revenue to $4.93–4.95B vs about $5.11B expected, trimmed its full-year revenue range to $23.08–23.37B and agreed to sell **Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68B** (company release, Seeking Alpha). The shares fell about 11–12% after hours (Yahoo Finance, Seeking Alpha). Ross Stores earned $1.91 vs $1.87 expected on revenue of $6.26B with comparable sales +8%, and raised its full-year EPS outlook, but fell about 9–10% after hours on a softer next-quarter guide (StockStory, StockTitan). Gap's comparable sales were flat (Old Navy flat, Gap +9%, Athleta −15%) and it cut its adjusted EPS outlook to $2.29–2.34 from $2.35–2.45 (company release via StockTitan, Bloomberg). Keysight's revenue jumped 41% to $1.99B with non-GAAP EPS of $3.61, and it guided Q1 to $2.04–2.06B (SEC filing). Earlier Walmart slipped despite beating and raising its outlook (EconCurrents). BJ's reports Friday morning.

stories.title: Nvidia falls a sixth day; board shuts the door on Huang.
stories.body: Nvidia fell another **3.3%** Thursday (StockTitan), after sliding 2.9% Wednesday to $150.96 despite its fiscal Q3 beat: revenue **$115.8B** (+103%, data center $107.6B) vs about $109B expected, non-GAAP EPS **$2.68** vs about $2.47, and a January-quarter guide of **$130B ±3%** vs about $125B (company release, CoinDesk). Reuters cited Nvidia's leadership change and shrinking data-center capex bets among the day's weights on tech. The board added $150B to the buyback (Newsquawk). Chairman Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO; the WSJ reported the SEC is looking at whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors (via TheStreet). Polymarket now gives about 5% that Huang rejoins by Dec 31 and about 20% that a permanent CEO is named by then (last trade Monday), with Arm's Rene Haas the favourite at about 28%.

stories.title: Oil ends flat as Hormuz attacks offset a supply glut.
stories.body: December WTI slipped 0.06% to settle at **$83.21** and Brent rose 0.03% to **$91.98** Thursday after swinging in a $2 range; the more active January WTI settled at $82.44 (Bloomberg via Rigzone). Traders weighed renewed Iran tensions, with Western officials saying the chances of new US strikes had grown and President Trump telling Axios he was not "rushing into a decision", plus Iran's navy saying two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz (not independently verified), against a 3.4 million-barrel US crude build and forecasts of a surplus (Reuters, Bloomberg via Rigzone). Flows through Hormuz are at a record, according to the US energy chief, and China's imports are rebounding faster than expected. Crude is down about a fifth in November; the December WTI contract expires Friday and OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
